guides.title: Lisbon
guides.why: Portugal's capital, spread over steep hills above the River Tagus. Much of it was rebuilt after the great earthquake of 1755.
lookFor: The yellow trams squeezing through streets barely wider than they are.
Patterned pavements of small black and white stones (calçada).
facts: On 1 November 1755 an earthquake, a tsunami and fires destroyed much of the city.
The flat grid of the Baixa was laid out afterwards under the Marquis of Pombal.

kids.q: Why do so many buildings have tiles on the outside?
kids.a: Glazed tiles (azulejos) are tough, easy to clean and keep walls cool. They are a Lisbon speciality.

guides.title: São Jorge Castle
guides.why: A hilltop fortress over the old town, with the best view in Lisbon. People have fortified this hill for well over two thousand years.
lookFor: The view across the rooftops to the river from the walls.
facts: The Moorish castle was captured in 1147 by Afonso Henriques, Portugal's first king, with help from crusaders.
It served as a royal palace until the early 1500s, when the kings moved to a new palace by the river.

kids.q: How many towers can you count from the main courtyard?
kids.a: Count them as you walk the walls. There are more than ten.

guides.title: Jerónimos Monastery
guides.why: A huge, lace-like monastery paid for by the riches of Portugal's sea voyages. It's the masterpiece of the Manueline style.
lookFor: Ropes, shells and sea creatures carved into the stone of the cloister.
Vasco da Gama's tomb just inside the church.
facts: King Manuel I began building it around 1501.
It and Belém Tower became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.

kids.q: Why would a church be decorated with ropes and knots?
kids.a: They celebrate the sailors and ships that made Portugal rich.

guides.title: Belém Tower
guides.why: A small fortress at the edge of the river that guarded the way into Lisbon. It was the last thing sailors saw as they left.
lookFor: A stone rhinoceros head carved under one of the turrets.
Stone ropes knotted around the walls.
facts: It was built between about 1514 and 1519.
The rhinoceros is thought to recall the one sent from India to Lisbon in 1515.

kids.a: Look up under the turrets on the west side. It's one of the first rhinos ever carved in Europe.
